newsitem.title: GERMANY: German cash coffee trade slow as futures retreat.
newsitem.headline: German cash coffee trade slow as futures retreat.

text.p: German coffee roasters are hoping for further falls in futures and remain sidelined amid a bearish market tone, traders said on Monday.
"Coffee physicals are extremely slow now that the market has received encouraging supply news and the crop weather in Brazil has not generated any fears of damage," one said.
"Roasters and traders also appear adequately covered and there is an overall feeling we've seen the worst of any tightness for the time being."

Futures are in an extended retracement to the downside after they hit 20-year highs last month. New York July arabicas tumbled by some 38 percent over the last two weeks and on Friday closed at 195.10 cents/lb.

The opening of export registrations for July and August by Colombia, Germany's leading supplier, and U.S. government figures projecting both a higher Brazilian and world coffee crop in 1997/98 were boosting consumers' bargaining position.
But retail sales were generally weak after consumers hoarded supplies ahead of the implementation of coffee price hikes carried out by roasters to offset higher costs.
Roaster Tchibo in the latest of such moves last Thursday announced its retail prices would go up by an average 1.40 marks per kilo from June 26.
Importers said origin sellers were raising distant differentials to offset the impact of drastically lower world prices, but spot differentials were still firm.
Business was restricted to Brazilian and Central American new crop.
Brazils for July/August shipment cost $180 per 50 kg fob second hand, down $37 on the week and down $77 on the fortnight.
Colombia Excelso was $250, down $47 on the week and down $119 on the fortnight. Vietnam robustas were $80 cif, down $6 and $37 respectively.
